items.labelEn: Time since the extinction of the dinosaurs (end of the Cretaceous)
items.labelFr: Temps écoulé depuis l'extinction des dinosaures (fin du Crétacé)
items.conditions: Age of the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary (base of the Danian stage), when the non-avian dinosaurs died out. Numerical age on the ICS chart, in millions of years before present.
items.conditionsFr: Âge de la limite Crétacé–Paléogène (base de l'étage danien), quand les dinosaures non aviens ont disparu. Âge numérique de la charte de l'ICS, en millions d'années avant le présent.
items.locator: Chart, Cenozoic column: Paleocene, Danian stage, lower boundary numerical age (Ma)
items.confidenceNotes: The chart gives 66.00 Ma with no uncertainty. Linking the boundary to the dinosaur extinction is general knowledge, not stated on the chart. Chart notes that numerical ages are subject to revision.

calculation.formula: 538.8 Ma - 486.85 Ma = 51.95 Ma; low/high = worst-case sum of the two boundary uncertainties (±2.1 Ma)

items.conditions: From the base of the Cambrian (538.8 ± 0.6 Ma) to the base of the Ordovician (486.85 ± 1.5 Ma), ICS chart v2026/06.
items.conditionsFr: De la base du Cambrien (538,8 ± 0,6 Ma) à la base de l'Ordovicien (486,85 ± 1,5 Ma), charte de l'ICS v2026/06.
items.locator: Chart, Paleozoic column: base of Fortunian (Cambrian) and base of Tremadocian (Ordovician)
items.confidenceNotes: Low/high combine both uncertainties linearly (conservative). The two numbers are separate chart cells; the quote joins them with an ellipsis. Older charts gave a different Ordovician base (485.4 Ma).

calculation.formula: 251.902 Ma - 66.00 Ma = 185.902 Ma; low/high from the ±0.024 Ma Triassic-base uncertainty only

items.labelEn: Length of the Mesozoic era (age of dinosaurs)
items.labelFr: Durée de l'ère mésozoïque (l'âge des dinosaures)
items.conditions: From the base of the Triassic (251.902 ± 0.024 Ma) to the base of the Paleogene (66.00 Ma), ICS chart v2026/06.
items.conditionsFr: De la base du Trias (251,902 ± 0,024 Ma) à la base du Paléogène (66,00 Ma), charte de l'ICS v2026/06.
items.locator: Chart, Mesozoic column: base of Induan (Triassic); Cenozoic column: base of Danian
items.confidenceNotes: The range is narrow only because the chart gives no uncertainty for 66.00 Ma; the true uncertainty is larger. Display as about 186 million years.

items.labelEn: Time since the end of the last ice age's peak (Last Glacial Maximum)
items.labelFr: Temps écoulé depuis la fin du dernier maximum glaciaire
items.conditions: Ice sheets stood at their largest extent from 26.5 ka until 19–20 ka, when northern deglaciation began. Value is the midpoint of the 19–20 ka end date (ka = thousands of years ago).
items.conditionsFr: Les calottes glaciaires sont restées à leur extension maximale de 26 500 à 19 000–20 000 ans avant le présent, puis la déglaciation de l'hémisphère Nord a commencé. Valeur : milieu de la fourchette 19 000–20 000 ans.
items.quote: Nearly all ice sheets were at their LGM positions from 26.5 ka to 19 to 20 ka
items.confidenceNotes: 19 500 is a midpoint we chose, not a value in the source. Based on 5704 radiocarbon, Be-10 and He-3 ages. 'ka' is read as before present; the abstract does not state the reference year, and the difference (decades) is negligible. The LGM itself lasted about 26.5 to 19–20 ka. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value = middle of the published "19 to 20 ka"; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Age of the oldest known piece of the Earth (a Jack Hills zircon crystal)
items.labelFr: Âge du plus vieux fragment de Terre connu (un cristal de zircon des Jack Hills)
items.conditions: Uranium–lead age of a detrital zircon grain from the Jack Hills, Western Australia. It is a single crystal, not a whole rock.
items.conditionsFr: Âge uranium–plomb d'un grain de zircon détritique des Jack Hills (Australie-Occidentale). C'est un cristal isolé, pas une roche entière.
items.quote: the discovery of a detrital zircon with an age as old as 4,404+/-8 Myr
items.confidenceNotes: Low/high from the stated ±8 Myr. Same abstract gives 4,030 Myr for the oldest known rock components (Acasta Gneiss, Canada). NASA Earth Observatory gives '4.4 billion years'. A 2014 atom-probe study confirming the age was not opened.

items.labelEn: Age of the oldest known Homo sapiens fossils
items.labelFr: Âge des plus anciens fossiles connus d'Homo sapiens
items.conditions: Thermoluminescence age of heated flint tools found with H. sapiens remains at Jebel Irhoud, Morocco (weighted average ± uncertainty).
items.conditionsFr: Âge par thermoluminescence de silex chauffés trouvés avec des restes d'Homo sapiens à Jebel Irhoud (Maroc) ; moyenne pondérée ± incertitude.
items.quote: A weighted average age places these Middle Stone Age artefacts and fossils at 315 ± 34 thousand years ago.
items.confidenceNotes: Low/high from ±34 ka. A tooth from the site gives 286 ± 32 ka (same abstract). Smithsonian Human Origins rounds to 'About 300,000 years ago'. Classifying these fossils as H. sapiens is debated by some researchers.

items.labelEn: Age of the Great Pyramid of Giza
items.labelFr: Âge de la grande pyramide de Gizeh
items.conditions: Years from the reign of King Khufu (ca. 2551–2528 BC, Met Museum chronology), who built the pyramid, to 2026. Value is the midpoint of the reign.
items.conditionsFr: Années écoulées entre le règne du roi Khéops (vers 2551–2528 av. J.-C., chronologie du Metropolitan Museum), qui fit bâtir la pyramide, et 2026. Valeur : milieu du règne.
items.quote: The Great Pyramid at Giza, which is the largest Egyptian pyramid, belongs to his son and successor, Khufu (r. ca. 2551–2528 B.C.).
items.confidenceNotes: Egyptian chronologies differ: other references place Khufu decades earlier (e.g. 2589–2566 BC), so the true uncertainty is about a century, larger than low/high. Midpoint chosen by us. Mark as about 4,500 years.

items.labelEn: Time since the first writing (cuneiform, Mesopotamia)
items.labelFr: Temps écoulé depuis la première écriture (cunéiforme, Mésopotamie)
items.conditions: Years from the earliest stage of cuneiform (3200–3000 BC, Uruk, southern Iraq) to 2026. Value uses the start of that stage.
items.conditionsFr: Années écoulées entre les premiers temps de l'écriture cunéiforme (3200–3000 av. J.-C., Uruk, sud de l'Irak) et 2026. Valeur : début de cette phase.
items.locator: Essay, paragraph on the rebus principle
items.quote: Only a few examples of its use exist in the earliest stages of cuneiform from between 3200 and 3000 B.C.
items.confidenceNotes: The sentence is about the rebus principle but dates the earliest stages of cuneiform. The same essay says proto-cuneiform may have existed in Syria and Turkey as early as the mid-fourth millennium BC, so writing may be older. Dates are approximate ('ca.').

items.labelEn: Time since the Gutenberg Bible (start of printing in Europe)
items.labelFr: Temps écoulé depuis la Bible de Gutenberg (début de l'imprimerie en Europe)
items.conditions: Years from about 1455, when the first copies of the Gutenberg Bible (Mainz) became available, to 2026.
items.conditionsFr: Années écoulées depuis 1455 environ, date à laquelle les premiers exemplaires de la Bible de Gutenberg (Mayence) furent disponibles, jusqu'en 2026.
items.quote: Approximately 180 copies of the Gutenberg Bible were printed and first made available in about 1455.
items.confidenceNotes: 'About 1455' per the Library of Congress; other libraries say 1454–1455 (not opened). Gutenberg was printing before the Bible, so this is not the exact invention date of the press. Uncertainty about ±1 year.

items.labelEn: How fast a visual afterimage in memory fades (iconic memory)
items.labelFr: Vitesse d'effacement de l'image visuelle en mémoire (mémoire iconique)
items.conditions: Decay time constant of iconic (visual sensory) memory in human observers after a brief display, measured with a mask; other methods give up to 400 ms.
items.conditionsFr: Constante de temps d'effacement de la mémoire iconique (mémoire sensorielle visuelle) chez l'humain après une présentation brève, mesurée avec un masque ; d'autres méthodes donnent jusqu'à 400 ms.
items.locator: Introduction (citing Loftus et al. and ref. 23)
items.quote: iconic memory decayed with a time constant of around 100 ms, although studies using other procedures observed longer time constants, up to 400 ms
items.confidenceNotes: Secondary statement in a CC BY paper about monkeys; the human values come from the works it cites, which were not opened. A time constant is not the full lifetime: the same paper says a cue delay of 'a few hundred milliseconds' (Sperling 1960) wipes out the benefit. Sperling 1960 itself was not opened.

items.labelEn: How long a short-term memory lasts without rehearsal
items.labelFr: Durée d'un souvenir à court terme sans répétition mentale
items.conditions: Peterson & Peterson (1959): three-letter trigrams, rehearsal prevented; recall fell from about 80 % at 3 s to about 10 % at 18 s. Adults, laboratory.
items.conditionsFr: Peterson et Peterson (1959) : trigrammes de trois lettres, répétition mentale empêchée ; le rappel passe d'environ 80 % à 3 s à environ 10 % à 18 s. Adultes, en laboratoire.
items.locator: Section on short-term memory (Atkinson–Shiffrin model), paragraph on decay and interference
items.quote: Participants remembered about 80% of the trigrams after a 3-second delay, but only 10% after a delay of 18 seconds
items.confidenceNotes: Textbook account of the 1959 study; the original was not opened (paywalled). 18 s is the longest delay tested, not a measured 'lifetime'. The same page notes Keppel & Underwood (1962) attributed much of the loss to interference, not decay, and gives a general STM duration of 15 to 30 seconds. Source is CC BY-NC-SA: reference only.

items.labelEn: The attentional blink: blind spot after noticing something
items.labelFr: Le clignement attentionnel : angle mort après avoir repéré quelque chose
items.conditions: In a rapid stream of images, a second target is often missed if it comes 200–500 ms after the first one. Value is the end of that window.
items.conditionsFr: Dans un flux rapide d'images, une seconde cible passe souvent inaperçue si elle arrive 200 à 500 ms après la première. Valeur : fin de cette fenêtre.
items.quote: a reduced ability to report the second of two targets … if it appears within 200-500 msec of Target 1 (T1)
items.confidenceNotes: Review summarising many rapid-serial-visual-presentation studies; the exact window depends on the task. Value = upper end of the window (how long the blink lasts), low = start of the deficit window.

items.labelFr: Une fixation de l'œil pendant la lecture
items.conditions: Average duration of a fixation (eye still on one word) during silent reading by skilled adult readers.
items.conditionsFr: Durée moyenne d'une fixation (l'œil immobile sur un mot) pendant la lecture silencieuse chez des lecteurs adultes expérimentés.
items.quote: Fixations are short periods of time, which on average last approximately 250 ms
items.confidenceNotes: Review value; individual fixations vary widely, and other reviews give 200–250 ms (not opened). No range given in this source, so low/high are left null.

calculation.formula: median of per-subject mean durations in Table 5 (31.52, 31.44, 56.17, 47.95, 36.85, 44.94, 68.22, 49.41, 43.91 ms) = 44.94 ms; low/high = min/max

items.conditions: Median of the nine per-subject mean durations for saccades averaging about 9 degrees of amplitude; 9 healthy adults aged 24–39. Low/high = lowest and highest subject means.
items.conditionsFr: Médiane des durées moyennes de neuf sujets pour des saccades d'environ 9 degrés d'amplitude en moyenne ; 9 adultes en bonne santé de 24 à 39 ans. Bornes = plus faible et plus forte moyenne individuelle.
items.locator: Table 5, Statistics of Saccadic Parameters (Exp. 1.1), Duration [ms] column
items.confidenceNotes: Saccade duration grows with amplitude (main sequence), so this applies to ~9° jumps only; per-subject SDs are about 15–28 ms. Duration also depends on the detection threshold and sampling rate (discussed in the paper). Purves et al., Neuroscience 2e (NCBI Bookshelf NBK10991) gives 'on the order of 15–100 ms', consistent with this.

items.labelEn: Pause before answering in a conversation
items.labelFr: Pause avant de répondre dans une conversation
items.conditions: Median gap between the end of a yes/no question and the start of the answer, across 10 languages (video recordings of natural conversation). Low/high = range of the language medians.
items.conditionsFr: Écart médian entre la fin d'une question fermée et le début de la réponse, dans 10 langues (enregistrements vidéo de conversations naturelles). Bornes = plage des médianes par langue.
items.locator: Results, paragraph on Fig. 1 and Table S3
items.quote: ranging from 0 ms (English, Japanese, Tzeltal, and Yélî-Dnye) to +300 ms (Danish, ‡Ākhoe Hai‖om, Lao) (overall cross-linguistic median +100 ms)
items.confidenceNotes: Overall mode is 0 ms; language means range from +7 ms (Japanese) to +469 ms (Danish). The popular '~200 ms' summary matches the reported mode window (0–200 ms), not the median. Question–answer pairs only.
